chemistry-killer-01.title: States of Matter: Solid, Liquid, and Gas
chemistry-killer-01.topic: States of Matter: Solid, Liquid, and Gas
chemistry-killer-01.goal: Analyze the principles of States of Matter: Solid, Liquid, and Gas and deduce the correct conclusion under given conditions.
chemistry-killer-01.material:
Dem do experiment wey dem react copper (Cu) powder with oxygen ($\mathrm{O_2}$) inside closed container to make copper(II) oxide ($\mathrm{CuO}$). For all di experiments, di $\mathrm{O_2}$ inside di container na 2.0 g, and di reaction na $\mathrm{2Cu + O_2 \rightarrow 2CuO}$. Di mass of CuO wey form after di reaction na as follows.
(I) Cu 4.0 g → CuO 5.0 g
(II) Cu 8.0 g → CuO 10.0 g
(III) Cu 12.0 g → CuO 10.0 g
If di law of definite proportions dey hold for di same conditions, which one na di correct result wen 14.0 g of Cu and 4.0 g of $\mathrm{O_2}$ react inside di same container until one reactant finish completely?
chemistry-killer-01.thinking.0: States of Matter: Solid, Liquid, and Gas
chemistry-killer-01.s.s1.prompt:
Dem do experiment wey dem react copper (Cu) powder with oxygen ($\mathrm{O_2}$) inside closed container to make copper(II) oxide ($\mathrm{CuO}$). For all di experiments, di $\mathrm{O_2}$ inside di container na 2.0 g, and di reaction na $\mathrm{2Cu + O_2 \rightarrow 2CuO}$. Di mass of CuO wey form after di reaction na as follows.
(I) Cu 4.0 g → CuO 5.0 g
(II) Cu 8.0 g → CuO 10.0 g
(III) Cu 12.0 g → CuO 10.0 g
If di law of definite proportions dey hold for di same conditions, which one na di correct result wen 14.0 g of Cu and 4.0 g of $\mathrm{O_2}$ react inside di same container until one reactant finish completely?
chemistry-killer-01.s.s1.explain:
Step 1: For (III), even though Cu increase, CuO no increase pass 10.0 g, so na case wey all di 2.0 g of $\mathrm{O_2}$ inside di container don react, so CuO 10.0 g = Cu 8.0 g + O 2.0 g, dat means Cu:O = 4:1 (check: for (I) Cu 4.0 g + O 1.0 g = 5.0 g so O remain, for (II) Cu 8.0 g + O 2.0 g = 10.0 g so e no get excess or shortage, and for (III) Cu 4.0 g remain).
Step 2: Mass of O wey go react completely with Cu 14.0 g = $14.0 \times \frac{1}{4} = 3.5$ g. Di 4.0 g of $\mathrm{O_2}$ wey dem supply pass dat, so all di Cu react and $\mathrm{O_2}$ remain $4.0-3.5=0.5$ g.
Step 3: CuO wey form = 14.0 + 3.5 = 17.5 g (conservation of mass, ratio Cu:O:CuO = 4:1:5).
So di correct answer na a: CuO 17.5 g form, $\mathrm{O_2}$ 0.5 g remain. (Wrong answers: di total 18.0 g na value wey include O wey no react, and 20.0 g na value wey dem calculate based on O 4.0 g and ignore di shortage of Cu)
chemistry-killer-01.s.s2.prompt: Which scenario demonstrates the correct real-world application of this principle?
chemistry-killer-01.s.s2.explain: The fundamental principles of this inquiry are widely implemented in modern technology.
chemistry-killer-01.s.s1.hint.0: For (III) wey Cu remain, di 10.0 g of CuO get all di 2.0 g of O wey dey inside di container → find di mass ratio Cu:O, den compare which one no reach. Mass of product = mass of Cu wey react + mass of O wey react.
chemistry-killer-01.s.s1.hint.1: (III): CuO 10.0 g = Cu 8.0 g + O 2.0 g → mass ratio Cu:O = 4:1. Di O wey go react with Cu 14.0 g na $14.0 \times \frac{1}{4} = 3.5$ g < 4.0 g, so Cu na di limiting reactant.
